title: Choose the visual world
question: Fresh hand for Zulfekar's portfolio — four directions from the sculptor's and studio's world, none repeating the rejected render-pass system. Pick one, re-roll, or play it straight.

options.label: THE CLAY STUDIO
options.thesis: A sculptor's studio: every subject is a white-clay maquette on a turntable under one spotlight, the portfolio as a bench of works in progress.
options.viewport: Warm studio ground. Left: the name as monumental type on a clay-textured panel with the title in inventory mono. Right: the photo on a turntable stand under a visible spotlight cone; hovering rotates the stand. Work appears as a bench of maquettes below.
options.risk: Warm and light reads approachable — it must stay disciplined, not cozy.

options.label: THE DAILIES SHEET
options.thesis: A production handoff document: the portfolio is a dailies review sheet with a title block, reference stills, and an approval stamp that earns contact.
options.viewport: Paper sheet fills the viewport: a title block with the name and credentials top-left, the photo as a stamped 'REFERENCE STILL' frame, the skills as a shot list with frame numbers, and the contact CTA as an 'APPROVED — HANDOFF' stamp in red.
options.risk: A document world can feel flat if the sheet never gets texture and density; it must be a real sheet, not a white page.

options.label: THE BLUEPRINT
options.thesis: A drafting sheet: the artist as an engineer of form, every section dimensioned and annotated like a construction drawing.
options.viewport: Deep blueprint blue ground with white drafting lines. Top-left a title block with the name; the photo sits in a 'SECTION A-A' frame with dimension lines running across the viewport; sections carry measurement callouts that animate when hovered.
options.risk: Blueprint is the most technical read — clients get it last; the contact action must still pop in drafting red.

options.label: THE WHITE CUBE
options.thesis: A gallery at night: the artist's work as artifacts on plinths under spotlights, the visitor walking a lit exhibition.
options.viewport: Near-black gallery wall. Top: the name engraved on a brass wall plate with a halo of light. Below: each project a concrete plinth with an honest un-plated monolith and its label card, the visitor's path down the gallery; one plinth always carries the action.
options.risk: Dark-with-spotlight must stay museum, not nightclub: warm tungsten, zero glow effects.

options.label: RENDER PASSES
options.thesis: The page as a composited render with a pass switch — the roll's original assignment.
options.viewport: Viewport chrome, layer-stack panel, pass-view switch.
options.risk: You reviewed it and passed: the pass vocabulary stayed too abstract for the page to land.
options.kept: Mono measurement readouts and honest empty states stay worth keeping in any world.
